```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5.5, dpi = 120)
source("../R/_load.R")
```

County-level estimates, spatial weights, global and local spatial autocorrelation, hot spots, empirical Bayes smoothing and an exploratory spatial regression. County estimates are design-based; counties with fewer women than `analysis.small_county_n` are flagged as imprecise.

```{r load}
df <- readRDS(file.path(cfg$paths$out, "data", "analysis_data.rds"))
bnd <- read_boundaries(cfg); bnd <- match_boundaries(bnd, unique(df$county[df$in_sample]), cfg)
est <- county_estimates(df, cfg)
bnd <- bnd[match(est$county_key, bnd$county_key), ]       # same order as the estimates
nbs <- build_neighbours(bnd, cfg); nsim <- cfg$spatial$permutations
save_table(est, "05_county_estimates", cfg)
knitr::kable(head(est[order(-est$pct), c("county", "n", "pct", "low", "high", "small_n")], 10), digits = 1, caption = "Highest ten counties")
```

## Neighbourhood structure

```{r nb}
summary(spdep::card(nbs$nb))
```

## Global Moran's I

```{r moran}
gm <- global_moran(est$pct, nbs$lw, nsim, cfg$project$seed); save_table(gm, "05_global_moran", cfg); knitr::kable(gm, digits = 4)
```

## Local Moran's I (LISA) and Getis-Ord Gi*

```{r lisa}
lisa <- local_moran(est$pct, nbs$lw, nsim, cfg$spatial$lisa_alpha, cfg$project$seed)
gi   <- getis_ord(est$pct, nbs$nb, cfg$spatial$lisa_alpha)
res  <- bind_cols(est, lisa, gi); save_table(res, "05_lisa_gistar", cfg)
knitr::kable(table(LISA = lisa$cluster, `Gi*` = gi$hotspot))
```

Cluster labels use the unadjusted permutation p value. The columns `cluster_fdr` and `hotspot_fdr` apply a false discovery rate correction for the 47 simultaneous tests and are the conservative reading.

## Empirical Bayes smoothing

Small counties have unstable raw estimates. The smoothed values shrink them toward the national (global) or neighbourhood (local) mean.

```{r eb}
eb <- eb_smooth(est$pct / 100, est$n, nbs$nb); res <- bind_cols(res, eb); save_table(res, "05_county_spatial_results", cfg)
knitr::kable(head(res[order(res$n), c("county", "n", "pct", "eb_global", "eb_local")], 8), digits = 1)
```

## Do county effects cluster after adjustment?

Moran's I of the multilevel county random effects tells whether geography still carries signal once individual factors are removed.

```{r remoran}
fits <- readRDS(file.path(cfg$paths$out, "models", "glmm_fits.rds"))
re <- county_random_effects(fits$full)
rm <- re_moran(re, bnd, nbs$lw, nsim, cfg$project$seed); save_table(rm, "05_random_effect_moran", cfg); knitr::kable(rm, digits = 4)
```

## Exploratory county-level spatial regression

This ecological model relates county coverage to county context. It describes areas, not women, and with 47 counties it is exploratory.

```{r sreg}
ctx <- county_context(df, cfg)
d2 <- merge(est, ctx, by = c("county", "county_key")); d2 <- d2[match(bnd$county_key, d2$county_key), ]
sr <- spatial_regression(d2, nbs$lw, "pct", vapply(cfg$spatial$contextual, function(s) s$name, ""))
save_table(sr$compare, "05_spatial_model_comparison", cfg); save_table(sr$lm_tests, "05_lm_tests", cfg)
knitr::kable(sr$compare, digits = 3); knitr::kable(sr$lm_tests, digits = 4); knitr::kable(sr$resid_moran, digits = 4)
summary(sr$ols)
```

Read the Lagrange multiplier tests in the usual order: if only the lag test is significant, choose the lag model; if only the error test, the error model; if both, use the robust versions. If neither is significant, the ordinary least squares model is adequate.

```{r save}
saveRDS(list(bnd = bnd, res = res), file.path(cfg$paths$out, "data", "spatial_results.rds"))
```
